statement: To cut a given straight line so that the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the square on the remaining segment.
heath_proof: Let AB be the given straight line; thus it is required to cut AB so that the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the square on the remaining segment. For let the square ABDC be described on AB; [I. 46] let AC be bisected at the point E, and let BE be joined; let CA be drawn through to F, and let EF be made equal to BE; let the square FH be described on AF, and let GH be drawn through to K. I say that AB has been cut at H so as to make the rectangle contained by AB, BH equal to the square on AH. For, since the straight line AC has been bisected at E, and FA is added to it, the rectangle contained by CF, FA together with the square on AE is equal to the square on EF. [II. 6]  But EF is equal to EB; therefore the rectangle CF, FA together with the square on AE is equal to the square on EB. But the squares on BA, AE are equal to the square on EB, for the angle at A is right; [I. 47] therefore the rectangle CF, FA together with the square on AE is equal to the squares on BA, AE. Let the square on AE be subtracted from each; therefore the rectangle CF, FA which remains is equal to the square on AB. Now the rectangle CF, FA is FK, for AF is equal to FG; and the square on AB is AD; therefore FK is equal to AD. Let AK be subtracted from each; therefore FH which remains is equal to HD. And HD is the rectangle AB, BH, for AB is equal to BD; and FH is the square on AH; therefore the rectangle contained by AB, BH is equal to the square on HA. therefore the given straight line AB has been cut at H so as to make the rectangle contained by AB, BH equal to the square on HA. Q. E. F.

**Statement:** To cut a given straight line so that the rectangle contained by the whole and one of the segments is equal to the square on the remaining segment.

**Step 1.** Let AB be the given straight line. On AB describe the square ABDC [1.46]; its four sides are equal and its angles are right [D1.22].

**Step 2.** Bisect AC at the point E [1.10], and join BE [P1].

**Step 3.** Produce CA in a straight line through A to F [P2], and on the produced line cut off EF equal to EB [1.3].

**Step 4.** On AF describe the square AFGH [1.46]. Since the angle BAC is right and F lies on CA produced, the adjacent angle BAF is also right [1.13]; hence the side AH of the square AFGH, which stands at right angles to AF at A, lies along AB, so that H is a point of AB.

**Step 5.** Produce GH to meet CD at K [P2]. Then FCKG (call it FK) is a rectangle with sides CF and FG, and AHKC (call it AK) is a rectangle with sides AH and AC, common to FK and to the square AD.

**Step 6.** The straight line AC has been bisected at E, and the straight line AF has been added to it in a straight line. Therefore the rectangle contained by CF and FA together with the square on AE is equal to the square on EF [2.6].

**Step 7.** But EF is equal to EB (Step 3), so the square on EF is equal to the square on EB. Hence the rectangle CF·FA together with the square on AE is equal to the square on EB.

**Step 8.** Since the angle EAB, which is the angle CAB of the square, is right, in the right-angled triangle EAB the square on EB is equal to the squares on BA and AE together [1.47].

**Step 9.** Therefore the rectangle CF·FA together with the square on AE is equal to the squares on BA and AE together [CN1].

**Step 10.** Subtract the square on AE from each; the remainders are equal [CN3]. Therefore the rectangle CF·FA is equal to the square on AB.

**Step 11.** Now the rectangle CF·FA is the rectangle FK, for FG is equal to FA (sides of the square AFGH) and the angle at F is right, so that FK is contained by CF and FG [D2.1]. And the square on AB is the square AD. Therefore FK is equal to AD [CN1].

**Step 12.** From each subtract the rectangle AK, which is common to both; the remainders are equal [CN3]. Therefore the remainder FH, the square AFGH, is equal to the remainder HD, the rectangle HBDK.

**Step 13.** But HD is the rectangle contained by AB and BH, since BD is equal to AB (sides of the square ABDC) and the angle at B is right [D2.1]; and FH is the square on AH.

**Step 14.** Therefore the rectangle contained by AB and BH is equal to the square on AH [CN1]. Thus the given straight line AB has been cut at H so that the rectangle contained by the whole AB and the segment BH is equal to the square on the remaining segment AH. Q.E.F.
